channel.title: Dr. Nidhi Patel (M.S.) — Writing & Research
channel.description: The writing and research of Dr. Nidhi Sanjay Patel, M.S. (Ayurveda) in Prasuti Tantra & Stree Roga: dissertation, journal articles, conference abstracts and seminar notes. Free to read and download.

item.title: A Clinical Study of Lashuna Kalpa & Rasnadi Taila Uttar Basti in Artava Kshaya w.s.r. to Hypomenorrhoea
item.description: Artava Kshaya (hypomenorrhoea) is a common menstrual complaint in reproductive-age women and a frequent cause of fertility concern. This randomised clinical study was undertaken in the Department of Prasuti Tantra & Stree Roga, Dr. N.R.S. Govt. Ayurvedic College, Vijayawada, to evaluate the efficacy of Lashuna Kalpa and Rasnadi Taila administered by Uttar Basti in the management of Artava Kshaya w.s.r. to Hypomenorrhoea. item.title: Ayurveda for Public Health
item.description: Ayurveda is an ancient medical science of human civilisation and a holistic health science that addresses the individual as well as the community. Owing to severe pollution, climate change, population growth and other socio-economic pressures, the world today faces a strong survival strain on all living beings and on nature; maintaining the wholeness of nature and human health is a pressing obligation that cannot be ignored. item.title: Delivery of Intrauterine Growth Restriction (IUGR)
item.description: Intrauterine growth restriction is one of the most consequential complications of pregnancy, associated with elevated perinatal mortality and long-term neurodevelopmental impact. This seminar covers the aetiology and classification of fetal growth restriction, the antenatal surveillance methods including biophysical profile, amniotic fluid assessment, Doppler studies and the role of lung maturation, the significance of the L:S ratio and phosphatidylglycerol, and the timing and mode of delivery in the growth-restricted fetus. item.title: Role of Uttarbasti in Yonivyapada
item.description: Without Tridosha, no disease can form or manifest. Of the three, Kapha and Pitta are non-motile, while motility is attributed exclusively to Vata — and it therefore follows that vitiation of Kapha and Pitta most often requires an initiation from Vata Dosha. Basti has good therapeutic efficacy in normalising a vitiated Vata, which makes it a rational primary intervention in Yonivyapada, the umbrella term in Stri Roga covering almost all diseases of women. item.title: The Conceptual Approach of Preconceptional Care in Ayurveda
item.description: Preconceptional care in Ayurveda emphasises a holistic approach to ensuring optimal health before conception. Nature has given the human body the great responsibility of pregnancy, and in the present era, where lifestyle-related issues and environmental factors affect fertility, couples seeking a "Supraja" — a healthy, physically, mentally and intellectually strong child — are drawn to Ayurvedic principles. item.title: The Role of Panchakarma in Vandhyatwa (Female Infertility): A Comprehensive Review
item.description: Vandhyatwa (female infertility) is one of the most common yet least discussed clinical presentations in Prasuti Tantra. This comprehensive review evaluates the role of Panchakarma in the management of female infertility, examining both Shodhana (purificatory) and Shamana (palliative) approaches as described in classical texts. The review covers the indications for Virechana, Vamana, Basti and Nasya in the context of reproductive disorders, together with the role of Ahara (diet), Vihara (lifestyle) and Dinacharya as the foundational substrate of any fertility protocol. item.title: Abnormal Development of the Fallopian Tube and Ovary
item.description: Congenital anomalies of the fallopian tube and ovary are a significant and under-recognised cause of subfertility and recurrent pregnancy loss. This seminar traces the normal embryological development of the Müllerian and gonadal systems and the critical windows in which developmental errors occur, then classifies the congenital anomalies of the fallopian tube — including agenesia, hypoplasia, accessory tubes and tubal diverticula — and of the ovary, relating each to its effect on ovulation, tubal patency and fertility potential. item.title: Artava Kshaya (Oligohypomenorrhoea)
item.description: Artava Kshaya — scanty menstruation — is among the most under-reported complaints in Stree Roga, yet it is frequently the earliest signal of a fertility concern and is often dismissed by patients and clinicians alike. item.dc:creator: Dr. Nidhi Sanjay Patel

item.title: Complications of the Stages of Labour
item.description: This seminar covers the complications that may arise at each of the three stages of labour — the first, second and third — and their management in the Ayurvedic obstetric framework. It addresses abnormal progress and the recognition of obstructed and prolonged labour, the management of postpartum haemorrhage and the third-stage complications of retained placenta and uterine atony, and the indications for referral. item.title: Concept of Pathya in Relation to Prasuti Tantra & Stree Roga
item.description: In Vachaspata, the verse reads "pathya-pathe, marge, hite chikitsad-au, hitakarakabhoktryadravyabhedahe" — pathya is that which walks the path of benefit and is wholesome in ahi (food), vihara (conduct) and chikitsa (treatment). The word pathya derives from the root path, literally a way or channel. In Shabdakalpadrum, pathya is described as that which is beneficial to the patient, while apathya harms. item.title: Concepts of Rasa in Relation to Prasuti Tantra & Stree Roga
item.description: Rasa occupies a distinctive position in Ayurvedic pharmacology as the most refined and most potent preparation class, formed through shodhana, marana and bhavana processes. This seminar explores the concept of Rasa in relation to Prasuti Tantra and Stree Roga, tracing the classical definitions of rasa, the pharmacological action attributed to rasaushadhi, the relationship between rasa and agni, and the classical cautions governing their use across the reproductive life-cycle — particularly in pregnancy, where specific rasa preparations are contraindicated. item.title: Effect of Pumsavana Karma in Conception
item.description: Pumsavana Karma, the first of the Shodasha Samskaras, is performed to secure a healthy, intelligent and prosperous progeny — the classical aim of Suputrakameeya. The karma may be performed immediately prior to conception (Pushyanakshatra) and is directed at Garbhadharana (conception) and Garbhasthireekarana (the settling of the embryo). item.title: Epilepsy in Pregnancy
item.description: Epilepsy in pregnancy presents a dual therapeutic challenge: controlling seizures while avoiding harm to the fetus through medication, and managing the labour itself. This seminar reviews the epidemiology and classification of seizure disorders in pregnancy, the effect of pregnancy on seizure control, the principles of anti-epileptic drug management in the antenatal, intrapartum and postpartum periods including the teratogenic considerations, the management of eclampsia and status epilepticus, and the Ayurvedic understanding of the condition and its adjuvant role. item.title: Gestational Diabetes Mellitus
item.description: Gestational diabetes mellitus is now the commonest medical complication of pregnancy and carries substantial maternal and fetal consequences, including macrosomia, hypertensive disorders and neonatal hypoglycaemia. This seminar covers the screening and diagnostic criteria, the glucose targets and monitoring required, the nutritional and lifestyle management of the condition, the pharmacological options, the intrapartum and postpartum management, and the long-term risk of progression to type 2 diabetes. item.title: Prasava Vigyana — Ayurvedic Obstetrics
item.description: Prasava Vigyana is the classical science of management of labour. This seminar presents the Ayurvedic framework for the conduct of normal labour, working through the four stages of prajasma with their characteristic signs, the assessment of the onset of labour and the progress of the uterine contractions, the ahara-vihara and positional management advised in each stage, the use of the classical formulations indicated for each stage, and the management of the third stage including the prevention of postpartum haemorrhage and the care of the newborn. item.title: Role of Dinacharya for Immunity
item.description: Dinacharya is defined as the daily routine. According to Ayurveda, one should follow Dinacharya in order to lead a healthy and disease-free life. Ayurveda gives more emphasis on the prevention of disease than on its treatment, and Dinacharya is the practical vehicle for that principle: it establishes balance in one's constitution, regularises the biological clock, aids digestion, absorption and assimilation, and generates self-esteem, discipline, peace, happiness and longevity. item.title: Sadarasa in Prasuti Tantra & Stree Roga
item.description: Sadarasa — equipoise of mind — occupies a distinctive place in Ayurvedic theory, which holds that the mental component of disease is not an adjunct but a parallel axis of treatment. item.dc:creator: Dr. Nidhi Sanjay Patel

item.title: Vomiting in Pregnancy: Nausea and Vomiting of Pregnancy in Ayurveda
item.description: Nausea and vomiting of pregnancy is one of the earliest and most universal symptoms of gestation, described in the classical texts as Garbhini Chardi. This seminar presents the Ayurvedic understanding of vomiting in pregnancy, the doshic basis of the condition, the classical diagnostic and therapeutic approach, the role of Ahara-Vihara and the specific formulations indicated in pregnancy with their indications, precautions and rationales, and the differentiation from the pathological vomiting of later pregnancy such as hyperemesis gravidarum. item.title: Role of Dinacharya in the Prevention of Health Hazards of Pollution
item.description: This supervised compilation examines the role of Dinacharya — the classical daily regimen — in preventing the health hazards posed by pollution, in the Department of Swasthavritta, Parul Institute of Ayurveda, Parul University.
